introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2024. Duration: One Hour Forty Five Minutes.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Suppose a lady earns a net monthly income of 25,000 FCFA as a hairdresser but decides to abandon it to run a small restaurant. She withdraws 500,000 FCFA from her Credit Union account and invests in the restaurant project. The current monthly interest rate paid on savings in the Credit Union is 1%. She uses her house to run the restaurant that used to fetch her monthly rent of 10,000 FCFA. She incurs these other costs per month:

- Council rate: 10,000 FCFA
- Food and related items: 50,000 FCFA
- Water, electricity and other costs: 25,000 FCFA
- Detergents and related cleaning materials: 10,000 FCFA
- Salary of the worker she has employed: 15,000 FCFA

She makes a monthly income of 125,000 FCFA.
incertitudes: Question 2(d) : « the minimum income this lady needs to make to operate in the short run » n'a pas de réponse imprimée ; le corrigé retient les coûts explicites (110 000 FCFA) et signale en nuance le seuil de fermeture (coûts variables 100 000 FCFA, la taxe communale étant un coût fixe) et le seuil de long terme (150 000 FCFA). Le correcteur du Board peut attendre l'une ou l'autre de ces valeurs.

Question 2 : « monthly income of 125,000 FCFA » est interprété comme le chiffre d'affaires mensuel (recettes totales). Les coûts implicites sont : revenu de coiffeuse abandonné (25 000), intérêt de 1 % par mois sur 500 000 (5 000) et loyer abandonné (10 000) ; tous les calculs ont été refaits par script (explicites 110 000, implicites 40 000, bénéfice comptable 15 000, bénéfice économique -25 000). Points imprimés : (a) 2 + 2, (b) 8, (c) 3 + 3, (d) 2, soit 20.

La règle « Answer ANY THREE questions » est exprimée par `regles_choix` (3 sur 5, portée PAPER 3) ; la page de garde ne dit pas combien de questions figurent au sujet, le « 5 » est le nombre de questions imprimées (1 à 5). Aucun total de points n'est imprimé par question (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les points de chaque sous-question sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties ; la somme des points imprimés de chaque question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define:

(i) explicit costs. (2 marks)

(ii) implicit costs. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Explicit costs** are **the actual, out-of-pocket payments a firm makes to outsiders for the factors and inputs it hires or buys** (wages, rent, raw materials, electricity, taxes). They are paid in money and recorded in the firm's accounts, so they are also called accounting or money costs.

**(ii) Implicit costs** are **the opportunity costs of the resources that the owner of the firm supplies from his or her own stock** (own labour, own capital, own land or building), for which **no payment is made** and which do not appear in the accounts. They are measured by what those resources could have earned in their best alternative use (an imputed cost). Normal profit is an implicit cost.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the Lady's explicit and implicit costs. (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Explicit costs** (money actually paid out each month):

| Item | FCFA per month |
|---|---|
| Council rate | 10 000 |
| Food and related items | 50 000 |
| Water, electricity and other costs | 25 000 |
| Detergents and related cleaning materials | 10 000 |
| Salary of the worker | 15 000 |
| **Total explicit costs** | **110 000** |

$10\,000 + 50\,000 + 25\,000 + 10\,000 + 15\,000 = 110\,000$ FCFA.

**Implicit costs** (what the lady's own resources would have earned in their best alternative use):

| Item | Working | FCFA per month |
|---|---|---|
| Her own labour: income given up as a hairdresser | net monthly income | 25 000 |
| Her own capital: interest given up on the savings withdrawn | $1\% \times 500\,000$ | 5 000 |
| Her own house: rent given up | monthly rent | 10 000 |
| **Total implicit costs** | | **40 000** |

$25\,000 + 5\,000 + 10\,000 = 40\,000$ FCFA.

**Result: explicit costs = 110 000 FCFA; implicit costs = 40 000 FCFA** (so total economic cost = 150 000 FCFA per month).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate her:

(i) accounting profit. (3 marks)

(ii) economic profit. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Total revenue (monthly income) = 125 000 FCFA.

**(i) Accounting profit** = total revenue $-$ explicit costs

$= 125\,000 - 110\,000 = $ **15 000 FCFA per month**.

**(ii) Economic profit** = total revenue $-$ (explicit costs + implicit costs)

$= 125\,000 - (110\,000 + 40\,000) = 125\,000 - 150\,000 = $ **$-25\,000$ FCFA per month**, that is an **economic loss of 25 000 FCFA**.

**Interpretation.** The lady makes a positive accounting profit, but it is **less than normal profit**: she earns 15 000 FCFA from the restaurant, whereas her own resources earned 40 000 FCFA in their best alternative uses (hairdressing, interest and rent). She is therefore 25 000 FCFA per month worse off, and on this evidence she would be better off returning to hairdressing and keeping her savings and house in their previous uses.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is the minimum income this lady needs to make to operate in the short run? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
In the short run the lady's own resources are committed to the restaurant, so what she must at least recover is the money she actually pays out: she needs a minimum income equal to her **explicit costs, 110 000 FCFA per month**. At this income she breaks even in accounting terms (accounting profit is zero) and can continue to pay her worker, suppliers and the council.

(Refinement: the lowest income that makes it better to stay open than to close is her variable costs, $50\,000 + 25\,000 + 10\,000 + 15\,000 = 100\,000$ FCFA, since the council rate of 10 000 FCFA is a fixed cost. In the long run she needs 150 000 FCFA, i.e. explicit plus implicit costs, to earn normal profit and have zero economic profit.)
